lambda.rule: lam = |g_Q| / (2 e_target |g_L|): at an interior stationary point -g_Q + 2 lam e g_L = 0 so |e| <= |g_Q| / (2 lam |g_L|) = e_target

loop.message: CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL

probe.note: same theta, LU cache emptied and gc.collect() forced between solves; the growth is fitted over solves 2..n (solve 1 also pays for the model build and the jit compilation). The footprint is ri_phys_footprint from proc_pid_rusage, checked against vmmap --summary to 0.03 GB

memory.note: peak_gb is ru_maxrss of the process that MEASURED the block (monotone over a process, so a block's own peak is peak_gb_after minus the process high-water mark it started from); blocks marked reused=true carry the record of the chunk that measured them

stopping.name: the |grad| stop criterion (scipy tests the PROJECTED gradient)
stopping.message: CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL

O1.name: loss decreases over the accepted iterates

O3.name: final Q >= best sweep Q inside the 2 % L band
O3.statement: NO sweep point qualifies: none of the 27 forward solves of the 3x3x3 grid lands inside the 2 % L band

O4.name: jax.grad vs FD4 at the final theta (objective)

M1.name: physical footprint of every block within the limit it ran under, and the per-solve growth measured rather than assumed
M1.metric: ri_phys_footprint (proc_pid_rusage), NOT ru_maxrss -- see the study's section 0b: under memory pressure RSS falls while the process grows
